business_problem: Paradigm needed to extract and interpret complex medical-record information for clinical-trial enrollment faster and more accurately so providers could match patients to trials without overwhelming clinicians with manual review.
solution_summary: Paradigm replaced a slow patchwork of specialized healthcare ML and NLP models with GPT-4 delivered through the OpenAI API to analyze clinical-trial data and patient records. Instead of building, training, and validating a separate model for every data element, the company now uses GPT-4’s long context and multimodal capabilities to summarize unstructured medical text, identify relevant clinical details, and match patients against trial criteria. The system was evaluated on expert-curated golden datasets and outperformed state-of-the-art domain models by at least 10% on a blended precision/recall metric, with especially strong gains on complex information spread across multiple documents. Because the resulting output requires far less validation data and less manual checking from clinicians, Paradigm can expand faster to new providers and trials while moving toward interactive patient-eligibility conversations that further reduce burden on nurses and doctors.

solution_components.name: OpenAI API
solution_components.role: Provides the integration layer through which Paradigm processes medical records and trial data.

solution_components.name: GPT-4
solution_components.role: Extracts, interprets, and reasons over unstructured clinical data for trial matching and screening.

data_flow: Medical records, notes, and trial documents are passed through the OpenAI API to GPT-4, which extracts structured facts and eligibility signals from unstructured content. Paradigm then validates outputs against expert-curated datasets and uses the resulting matches to support clinicians and provider partners in enrollment workflows.
business_outcome: Paradigm accelerated its product roadmap, reduced clinician validation effort, improved extraction accuracy, and created a path to more equitable access to life-saving clinical trials for underserved patients.
